properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued August 3 at 8:14PM EDT until August 4 at 12:45AM EDT by NWS Blacksburg VA
properties.description:
At 814 PM EDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing heavy
rain across the warned area. Between 4 and 5 inches of rain have
fallen. The expected rainfall rate is 1 to 2 inches in 1 hour.
Additional rainfall amounts up to 1 inch are possible in the warned
area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Lynchburg...                       Bedford...
Glasgow...                         Big Island...
Forest...                          Montvale...
Sedalia...

This includes the following streams and drainages...
Bold Branch, Back Creek, Big Otter River and Back Run.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

When it is safe to do so, please send your reports of flooding,
including mudslides or flooded roads, to the National Weather
Service by calling toll free at 1...8 6 6...2 1 5...4 3 2 4. Reports
and pictures can also be shared on the National Weather Service
Blacksburg Facebook page and on X.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued August 3 at 8:13PM CDT until August 6 at 7:00AM CDT by NWS Corpus Christi TX
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Texas...

Nueces River Near Three Rivers affecting Live Oak County.

Nueces River Near Tilden affecting McMullen County.

For the Nueces River...including Cotulla, Tilden, Three Rivers,
Mathis, Bluntzer, Calallen...Major flooding is forecast.

- Forecast...The river is expected to fall below flood stage early
Thursday morning and continue falling to 12.8 feet Saturday
evening.
- Flood stage is 25.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 36.2
feet on 07/20/1990.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Even 6 inches of fast-moving flood water can knock you off your feet
and a depth of 2 feet will float your car. Never try to walk, swim,
or drive through such swift water. If you come upon flood waters,
stop, turn around and go another way.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/crp.

properties.description:

Locations impacted include...

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued August 3 at 5:13PM MST until August 3 at 8:15PM MST by NWS Tucson AZ
properties.description:
FFWTWC

The National Weather Service in Tucson has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Central Cochise County in southeastern Arizona...

* Until 815 PM MST.

* At 513 PM MST, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain a large portion of Cochise County, with the heaviest
rain extending from San Simon southwest towards Kansas Settlement
and Pearce-Sunsites. Another area of heavy rain has occurred in the
Tombstone area. Between 1 and 2 inches of rain have fallen.
Additional rainfall amount s up to 1 inch are possible in the
warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Sierra Vista, Willcox, Whetstone, Huachuca City, St. David,
Tombstone, Portal, Bowie, Dragoon, Pearce-Sunsites, Chiricahua
National Monument, Kartchner Caverns State Park, Fort Huachuca,
Cochise, Sunizona, Kansas Settlement, Rucker Canyon, Texas Canyon
and Paradise.

This includes the following highways...
Route 90 between mile markers 296 and 331. Route 80 between mile
markers 296 and 328...and between mile markers 400 and 413. Route 181
between mile markers 39 and 64. Route 191 between mile markers 31 and
89. Route 92 between mile markers 322 and 323. Interstate 10 between
mile markers 309 and 389. Route 82 between mile markers 48 and 67.
Route 186 between mile markers 327 and 359.

This includes the following Flash Flood Prone Locations...
Hwy 181 at Turkey Creek.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

In hilly terrain there are hundreds of low water crossings which are
potentially dangerous in heavy rain. Do not attempt to cross flooded
roads. Find an alternate route.

properties.headline: Special Marine Warning issued August 3 at 9:39PM EDT until August 3 at 10:45PM EDT by NWS Key West FL
properties.description:
SMWKEY

The National Weather Service in Key West has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
Hawk Channel and Straits of Florida from west end of Seven Mile
Bridge to 20 nm west of Dry Tortugas out 20 nm...
Gulf of America from west end of Seven Mile Bridge to Halfmoon
Shoal out to 5 fathoms...
Gulf of America including Dry Tortugas and Rebecca Shoal Channel...

* Until 1045 PM EDT.

* At 939 PM EDT, a strong thunderstorm was located over Twenty-Eight
Foot Shoal Light. The strong thunderstorm was nearly stationary.

HAZARD...Wind gusts 34 knots or greater.

SOURCE...National Weather Service Meteorologist.

IMPACT...Expect wind gusts in excess of 34 knots, suddenly higher
waves, frequent lightning, and heavy downpours.

* Locations in the warning include...
Twenty-Eight Foot Shoal Light.
properties.instruction:
Prepare for wind gusts in excess of 34 knots, steep and fast-building
seas, frequent lightning, and blinding downpours. Stay low or go
below, and make sure all on board are wearing life jackets.

Intense and continuous lightning is occurring with this storm. Stay
low, or go below. Lower VHF antenna, outriggers, fishing rods, and
umbrellas.

properties.description:

At 940 PM EDT, a cluster of strong thunderstorms with possible
waterspouts were located near Cosgrove Shoal Light. The strong
thunderstorms were nearly stationary.

HAZARD...Waterspouts and wind gusts 34 knots or greater.

SOURCE...National Weather Service Meteorologist.

IMPACT...Waterspouts can quickly form and capsize boats, cause
considerable damage to vessels and create suddenly higher
waves. Expect wind gusts in excess of 34 knots, suddenly
higher waves, frequent lightning, and heavy downpours.

Locations in the warning include...
Cosgrove Shoal Light.
properties.instruction:

seas, frequent lightning strikes, and blinding downpours. Stay low or
go below, and make sure all on board are wearing life jackets.

Intense and continuous lightning is occurring with this storm. If
